name: Article in a Weak Proper Name

entry.name: Article in a Weak Proper Name

1.definition: Realizes a conventional proper name that uses an article in ordinary argument position.

relatedConstructions.notes: A different dedicated syntactic host for the primary name use.

projection.target: The article forms part of the ordinary naming pattern, while a label or compound can omit it in a suitable form. Arbitrary replacement with a does not preserve the primary name use.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Names that come with the
curious.summary: Some names include the word the as part of the name, as in the Thames.
curious.body: In They crossed the Thames, the word the isn't an extra. It belongs to the way this name is used in an ordinary sentence. The name and the article go together. That differs from names that need nothing in front of them. The dictionary describes the article here as part of the ordinary naming pattern. A label or compound can leave it out in a suitable form, but arbitrarily swapping in a does not keep the main name use. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
curious.try: Think of another name you can't say without the. What happens if you drop it?

teacher.summary: Helps explain proper names that conventionally take an article.
teacher.explain: A weak proper name is a noun phrase in which a lexically conventional article combines with a name expression, as in the Thames. It realizes a conventional proper name in ordinary argument position. The article forms part of the ordinary naming pattern, while a label or compound can omit it in a suitable form. Arbitrary replacement with a does not preserve the primary name use. This dictionary contrasts this with strong proper names, which have no such article, and marks its analysis provisional.
teacher.terms: The and a are determinatives, often called articles. This dictionary’s weak proper name contrasts with strong proper name.

contrasts.note: Name with its conventional article, in argument position.

watch_for: A learner might leave out the before a name that conventionally has it.
A learner might replace the with a, though this dictionary says arbitrary replacement does not keep the name use.
teacher.activity: Students list names of places or things they know, and sort them into names with the and names without it. They check each list against a reference.
